speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. To better assess your bleeding risk, have you ever experienced prolonged bleeding after a cut or had any spontaneous bruising? Additionally, do you have a family history of easy bleeding or bruising?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the family history of joint swelling; this suggests a potential hemophilia A or B. Have you ever been told you have low factor levels, or have you required clotting factor replacement therapy in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A.

Based on your family history of joint swelling and your symptoms of prolonged bleeding and easy bruising, the pattern is highly consistent with an X-linked bleeding disorder. To confirm this, I need to see the results of your coagulation studies.

REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Factor VIII activity level.
REQUEST IMAGES: Previous MRI of joints showing hemarthrosis.
